newsitem.title: GERMANY: German media giant Kirch mulls succession - report.
newsitem.headline: German media giant Kirch mulls succession - report.

text.p: Bavarian media mogul Leo Kirch is considering transforming his business into a charitable foundation in a move that could prefigure a possible flotation, German magazine Der Spiegel reported on Sunday.

In a news release ahead of publication on Monday, the magazine said Kirch, now approaching his 70th birthday, was considering the move as a way of ensuring a smooth succession of the group that he now runs practically single-handedly.
It added that Kirch's son Thomas, 38, could later be offered a "leading role" in the business, but was not being mooted as an overall chief in the style of his father.
A spokesman for the Kirch group said it was making no comment on the report.

Kirch is currently locked in a dispute with rival media group Bertelsmann AG over the future direction of pay-TV channel Premiere, a battle seen as decisive in the development of subscription-based television in Germany.

Kirch owns 25 percent of Premiere, while Bertelsmann, with a 37.5 percent stake, has management control of the channel. Premiere earlier this month secured an injunction preventing Kirch's own DF1 digital channel from competing against it.
The Kirch group, currently built around a chain of mainly privately-held companies, has as one of its main assets an arsenal of broadcasting rights to top Hollywood feature films.
According to the Spiegel article, Kirch is concerned to ensure his empire should run smoothly if he ever becomes incapable of directly taking charge of its operations.
It said Kirch might seek to establish a "holding company" that would be responsible for the running of the business and might ultimately take it towards a public listing.

Kirch himself would settle for a background "partiarchal role" similar to that occupied by Bertelsmann's Reinhard Mohn after he turned his business into a shareholding company in the 1970s, it suggested, quoting unnamed sources.
The magazine also said that Kirch would soon announce that two Kirch insiders, TV executive Dieter Hahn and lawyer Klaus Piette, were being appointed as senior managers within the group.
